disclosed_facts.fact: Comstock discloses a "Data Center Opportunity": it is partnering with NextEra Energy Resources, LLC to provide natural gas for new power generation in the Western Haynesville to support hyperscaler data center development, with initial capacity of 2 gigawatts and potential expansion to 8 gigawatts. No contract terms, pricing, volumes or executed agreement are disclosed.

The 10-K states its Haynesville/Bossier acreage has access to growing Gulf Coast natural gas demand "related to LNG exports, expansion of power generation for data centers and the petrochemical industry" — a market-positioning statement with no data center customer, contract or revenue attached.

Primary disclosed asset base is upstream natural gas: 7.0 Tcfe of proved reserves with $4.5 billion PV-10 and 1,069,991 acres (802,769 net) prospective for the Haynesville and Bossier shales as of December 31, 2025 — no compute, interconnection or colocation assets disclosed.

Company-owned midstream (Pinnacle Gas Services LLC) consists of gas treating plants in Bethel and Marquez, Texas and 246 miles of high-pressure pipelines providing gathering and treating for Western Haynesville production — gas midstream infrastructure, not electrical substation or grid interconnection.

Sixth Street invested $600 million for a 27% non-controlling common equity interest in Pinnacle Gas Services, with Comstock retaining 73% and continuing to manage and operate Pinnacle under a management services agreement; proceeds retired $445 million of Pinnacle preferred equity and Pinnacle debt. Disclosure ties the investment to midstream services, not to any data center or compute counterparty.

Letter of intent with SOCAR under which SOCAR would acquire 20% of Comstock's Legacy Haynesville working interest, 15% of Western Haynesville (stepping down to 7.5%), and 15% of Comstock's 73% Pinnacle interest for $1.65 billion cash; the LOI only binds the parties to negotiate in good faith a definitive purchase and sale agreement. No data center or compute element disclosed.

Reported revenues are natural gas and oil sales ($288.2 million in Q2 2026) plus "gas services" ($63.5 million in Q2 2026); no revenue line is attributed to data centers, hyperscalers or compute-related power supply.

primary_business: Independent natural gas producer in the Haynesville/Bossier shales of North Louisiana and East Texas, with a company-owned gas gathering and treating midstream JV (Pinnacle Gas Services).
key_unknowns: No executed gas supply or power agreement with NextEra or any hyperscaler is disclosed — no term, volume, pricing, take-or-pay, or total contract value for the 2 GW initial / 8 GW potential data center power concept.

Stated objective to be the world's leading provider of Total AI/IT Solutions through a richer enterprise customer mix and broader adoption of the DCBBS architecture, with continued investment in technology leadership, manufacturing scale and global compliance.

Remaining performance obligations of $60.7 billion as of December 31, 2025 (vs. $15.1 billion at December 31, 2024), with committed contracts carrying a weighted-average duration of approximately five years.

Customers generally access the platform through multi-year committed contracts under which they purchase a specified amount of capacity on a take-or-pay basis over the contract term; a number of customers have expanded initial commitments by contracting for additional capacity.

Operated 43 data centers with over 850 MW of active power as of December 31, 2025 (up from 32 data centers / ~360 MW at YE2024 and 10 / ~70 MW at YE2023), with total contracted power capacity of approximately 3.1 GW expected to deploy in future periods.

Platform runs across a distributed network of purpose-built data centers interconnected through a proprietary global network backbone, largely near major metropolitan areas, designed for high-density AI infrastructure with enhanced access to power and liquid cooling.
Infrastructure development is primarily financed through asset-level debt supported by take-or-pay customer contracts, supplemented by corporate-level equity and debt financing.

$2.6 billion delayed draw term loan facility (DDTL 5.5 Facility) entered August 7, 2026 with JPMorgan as administrative agent, entered primarily to finance capital expenditures required to perform certain customer contracts, including acquisition of GPU servers and related infrastructure; draws available until December 2026, maturity September 1, 2031.

$3.1 billion delayed draw term loan facility (DDTL 5.0 Facility) entered May 15, 2026 with Morgan Stanley Senior Funding as administrative agent, entered primarily to finance capital expenditures required to perform certain customer contracts, including acquisition of GPU servers and related infrastructure; draws available until September 2026, maturity November 15, 2031.

Balance sheet as of June 30, 2026 shows property and equipment, net of $46,736 million (vs. $30,557 million at December 31, 2025) and operating lease right-of-use assets of $16,595 million (vs. $8,231 million), with deferred revenue of $2,686 million current and $7,006 million non-current.

Completed private offering on June 18, 2026 of $1,250 million 9.625% Senior Notes due 2032 and €2,000 million 8.500% Senior Notes due 2032; announced June 11, 2026 intent to offer $3.5 billion equivalent of senior notes for general corporate purposes including repayment of indebtedness.

Disclosed joint venture to acquire and develop a data center campus in New Jersey, with estimates of maximum funding exposure to fund potential construction and development costs identified as a forward-looking item.

Proprietary software layer — CoreWeave Mission Control orchestration/observability, Slurm on Kubernetes (SUNK), proprietary storage solutions and Weights & Biases developer tooling — plus acquisitions of Weights & Biases, OpenPipe, Marimo and Monolith AI; CoreWeave Cloud received a second SemiAnalysis Platinum ClusterMAX rating in 2025.
Customer base described as leading enterprises, AI labs and technology companies deploying AI at scale; an on-demand pay-as-you-go model is also offered alongside committed contracts.

disclosed_facts.fact: Fermi describes itself as building Project Matador, a hyperscale private power and AI infrastructure campus in the Texas Panhandle, designed to deliver up to 11 GW (potentially ~17 GW) of private generation capacity and support up to ~15 million sq ft of AI-ready hyperscale compute infrastructure; tenant rent and capacity allocation are expected to be based on reserved power capacity in kilowatts per month.
Site control secured via a 99-year ground lease with the Texas Tech University System on land described as large enough to house the next three largest AI infrastructure campuses by square footage.

As of December 31, 2025 the company reported securing site control and groundwater rights, completing early-stage engineering/site development, progressing permitting, advancing grid interconnection and fuel supply arrangements, and procuring certain long-lead power generation equipment.

Campus infrastructure plan includes on-site natural gas-fired generation, supplemental grid-supplied power, battery energy storage, solar for energy displacement, and longer-term nuclear baseload supply; two major fiber optic transmission corridors connect at the southern boundary of the campus, enabling co-located tenants low-latency connectivity to primary digital backbone networks.

Business model is to develop and LEASE powered shell campus space to hyperscale/compute-intensive tenants, and it may offer long-term ground leases to tenants that build their own powered shells on its land; the company intends to elect REIT status, with development/generation activities in taxable REIT subsidiaries.

Development-stage company formed January 2025 that has generated no revenue to date; does not expect operating revenues until definitive tenant lease agreements are executed and powered shells and on-site power capacity are delivered. Execution depends on converting tenant discussions into binding agreements.
